title: Build & Deploy to Vercel
description: Push a Next.js project to GitHub and deploy it to Vercel with environment variables.
problemStatement:
## Goal
Take any Next.js project (like the blog from Chapter 8) and deploy it live on Vercel.

### Steps
1. Initialize a Git repository if you haven't already (`git init`, commit your files).
2. Create a new repository on GitHub and push your code.
3. Go to [vercel.com](https://vercel.com) and sign up/in with your GitHub account.
4. Click **New Project**, select your repo.
5. Vercel automatically detects Next.js; review the settings (Framework Preset should be Next.js).
6. Add any environment variables your app uses (e.g., `DATABASE_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`) in the Environment Variables section.
7. Click **Deploy**.
8. Once deployed, visit the provided `.vercel.app` URL to verify your app works.
9. Optionally add a custom domain in the project dashboard.

### Verification
Your app is live on the internet. Navigating to the URL shows your pages, and API routes function correctly.
hints: If using a database like SQLite, note that Vercel's serverless functions have a read‑only filesystem – you'll need a hosted database (like PlanetScale, Supabase) for production.
Make sure your `next.config.js` doesn't contain localhost references for production URLs.
If you see build errors, check the build logs in the Vercel dashboard.
expectedOutput: A live URL pointing to your deployed Next.js application.
